circuits.title: Inverting amplifier, gain -3.6
circuits.description: One amplifier inverts and scales its input. VIN feeds the inverting input through RI, RF closes the loop from the output back to that node, and the non-inverting input is grounded. RI = 10 kΩ and RF = 36 kΩ give a gain of -3.6, turning a ±0.5 V input into about ±1.8 V. The supplies are ±12 V. The second amplifier is unused.
notes: The input source returns to GND.

circuits.title: Non-inverting amplifier with supply bypass
circuits.description: A non-inverting stage: VIN reaches the non-inverting input through RIN, RG runs from the inverting input to ground and RF from the output back to the inverting input, so RF and RG set the gain. A 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic capacitor bypasses VS+ to ground beside the part; a second bypasses VS- and is needed only with a dual supply (with one supply, VCC- is ground). The second amplifier is unused.

operation.text: TL081 is the single, TL082 the dual and TL084 the quad of one FET-input op amp family. The original grades are C, AC and BC (0 °C to 70 °C), I (-40 °C to 85 °C) and M (-55 °C to 125 °C); the A and B letters mark tighter offset limits. TL081H, TL082H and TL084H are a newer die: 1 mV typical offset, 20 V/µs slew rate, 940 µA per channel typical, an input range that includes the positive rail, 1.5 kV HBM ESD, internal EMI and RF filtering, and a -40 °C to 125 °C range. TL082IDR is the dual, I grade, in SOIC-8 on a 2500-piece reel.

An H in the grade position means the part uses the latest-flow die, covered by the TL08xH electrical table and its typical-characteristic graphs. Grades without H or M may come from either the legacy or the latest flow and are covered by the DC and AC tables for the original die. M parts are legacy-flow die specified from -55 °C to 125 °C. Within the original-die tables, NS and PS packages and all M parts keep the older figures (3 MHz bandwidth, 18 nV/√Hz noise, 10 V to 30 V supply), while every other part has 5.25 MHz and 37 nV/√Hz and runs from 4.5 V to 40 V.

The TL08xH has a FET input pair, a reference current, two bias voltages and class-AB control circuitry driving the output. The input stage tolerates being switched between channels, its common-mode range reaches the positive rail, and it settles well in multiplexed systems. VCC- serves as ground in a single-supply circuit.
Typical THD is 0.003%, which suits audio paths, and the typical slew rate is 20 V/µs.
The amplifiers are on whenever the supply is connected, and they work from one supply or from split supplies. The TL08xH turns on in 60 µs typical with a 40 V supply ramped faster than 0.3 V/µs.

Each input has clamp diodes to both supply rails. Limit the current to 10 mA or less for any input that can swing more than 0.5 V past a rail. Apart from NS and PS packages and M parts, the common-mode input may go 0.5 V beyond either rail without damage and the recommended input range runs from (VCC-) + 4 V to (VCC+) + 0.1 V; the TL08xH is specified for VCM from (VCC-) + 1.5 V to VCC+. The TL08xH output does not reverse phase when the input is overdriven.

The output survives a continuous short to ground on one amplifier of a package at a time. The TL08xH short-circuit current is ±26 mA typical, and it drives up to 300 pF of load capacitance; overshoot against capacitive load is given with RISO = 0 Ω and 50 Ω in series with the output.
Only the single TL081C in the 8-pin PS (SO) package brings out OFFSET N1 and OFFSET N2. Test figure 4 puts a potentiometer across them with the wiper returned to VCC- through 1.5 kΩ.

A single supply above 36 V, or a split supply beyond ±18 V, can damage the part permanently. Put a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor near each supply pin so that noise on a noisy or high-impedance supply does not couple into the amplifier.

Fit a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor from each supply pin to ground, as close to the part as possible; a single-supply circuit needs only the one on V+. Keep analog and digital grounds apart and watch where ground current flows; a ground plane on an inner layer spreads heat and cuts EMI pickup. Route inputs away from supply and output traces, crossing them at right angles where they must meet. Mount the external parts tight to the amplifier, with RF and RG right at the inverting pin to hold down stray capacitance, and keep input traces short: they pick up noise most readily. A driven low-impedance guard ring round critical traces reduces leakage from nearby traces at other potentials.

In the non-inverting example on a single-amplifier SOIC-8, RG and RF sit right at the inverting input pin, RIN at the non-inverting input, the VS+ bypass capacitor beside the VCC+ pin and the VS- bypass (dual supply only; ground for a single supply) beside the VCC- pin, with a ground plane on another layer.

Choose a supply wider than the signal ranges: scaling ±0.5 V to ±1.8 V, ±12 V is enough. The gain is -1.8 / 0.5 = -3.6. Resistors in the kilohm range keep the currents in the milliampere range; RI = 10 kΩ then needs RF = 36 kΩ.
Catalog versions: TL082 and TL084. Automotive (AEC-Q100) versions: TL082-Q1. Military (QML) versions: TL082M and TL084M.
